fieldMarks: Total length 309-373 mm; tail 39-68 mm, much shorter than other prairie dogs
Yellowish-buff coat mixed with blackish hairs; darker top of head, cheeks and eyebrows
Tail base matches the back, distal half grayish with grayish-white hairs at the tip
behavior: Colonies often small, under 50-100 animals, in territories of one adult male, one or more females and young
Most activity early morning and late afternoon in spring and summer
Inactive periods lasting months in winter; hibernation in some parts
Diet of grasses, forbs, sedges and shrubs
habitat: Gently sloping grasslands and semi-desert and montane shrublands at 4,600-12,000 ft.
range: Central Colorado to central Arizona, including part of southeastern Utah and much of northwestern New Mexico.

lookalikes.name: White-tailed prairie dog
lookalikes.howToTell: Pure white distal tail hairs versus grayish-white on Gunnison's.
